name: suggest_next_queries
description:
ALWAYS call this at the very END of every response, as the last thing you do. It shows 3 clickable follow-up questions so the student can continue with one tap.

This applies to EVERY turn, including short plain-text answers that use no other tool. It is the one deliberate exception to any rule that says a plain text response should not call tools. Do not skip it because the answer was short.

Call it after your explanation is complete - never before, and never instead of answering.

RULES:
- Provide exactly 3 suggestions.
- Write each one in the STUDENT'S voice, as a message they would send you (e.g. 'Show me a worked example of gradient descent', not 'Would you like a worked example?').
- Keep each under ~80 characters so it fits on a button.
- Make them concrete and specific to what was just discussed. Never generic filler like 'Tell me more'.
- The three must be meaningfully different from one another and must not repeat the student's previous question.
- Do NOT also list these suggestions in your text; the UI renders them as buttons.

queries.description: Exactly 3 short follow-up messages written in the student's voice.
